title: bug: the reload-hold banner (a13eb354) is not a routine presence line, so each hot reload of a task-holding seat pages every busy seat in #workers and #governors, the reloading seat included, and wakes a channel-filtered chat_wait
description:
Filed by architect-1dd28c7c from the daemon/proxy defect hunt (task-8f18d6fa).

PROBLEM
task-4ddbfb31 (a13eb354, DONE 2026-11-03) changed what a wrapper_restart deregister does for a task-holding seat. It now holds the seat's task instead of releasing it, and posts "🔌 <id> reloading (wrapper_restart); holding N task(s) for its relaunch until <iso>: <task>(<status>)" to #workers and #governors (packages/moe-daemon/src/state/workerLifecycle.ts ~202-205).
util/chatPayload.ts isRoutinePresenceLine (~27-42) recognises only two shapes: "<id> left (<reason>)" and "🔌 <id> deregistered (<reason>); (no tasks held)". So the hold banner is not a feed line. It also mentions nobody, and MentionRouter routes a system line with no mentions to every non-IDLE, non-DEAD seat (util/mentionRouter.ts ~255-267). That includes the reloading seat itself, which is still CODING with reloadHoldUntil set.
task-48edc21b's contract, pinned in tools/chatSystemFeed.test.ts, is that a deregistration banner which released no task and dropped no resource claim routes to nobody, adds no unread and wakes no parked chat_wait. The hold path releases nothing, so its banner belongs in that quiet class. The actionable paths are unaffected: an expired hold goes through deregisterWorker with the hold-expired reason (state/sweeps.ts runReloadHoldSweep), releases the task, and its "released N task" banner keeps routing.
Rate: .moe/messages/chan-15c8e232.jsonl (#governors) shows 4 "🔌 worker-… deregistered (wrapper_restart); released 1 task: …→WORKING" banners on 2026-11-03. Once a13eb354 runs live, each of those reloads becomes a hold banner that pages every busy seat twice. No hold banner appears in today's chat yet, because the live daemon predates the restage.

EVIDENCE: repro on HEAD 99cae90a (a descendant of 1558f141), in a git-archive snapshot outside the shared checkout. The test calls deregister_worker {reason: wrapper_restart} on a task-less seat and on a task-holding seat while a #governors-filtered chat_wait is parked. File: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-8f18d6fa/zzHuntUtil3.test.ts (copy into a snapshot's packages/moe-daemon/src/util/). Output: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-8f18d6fa/repro-output-util-99cae90a.txt.
Command: cd <snapshot>/packages/moe-daemon && npx vitest run src/util/zzHuntUtil3.test.ts
Observed:
#workers "🔌 worker-idle-seat deregistered (wrapper_restart); (no tasks held)" -> routed []
#governors "🔌 worker-idle-seat deregistered (wrapper_restart); (no tasks held)" -> routed []
#workers "🔌 worker-holder reloading (wrapper_restart); holding 1 task(s) for its relaunch until 2026-11-…" -> routed ["qa-busy","worker-busy","worker-holder"]
#governors "🔌 worker-holder reloading (wrapper_restart); holding 1 task(s) for its relaunch until 2026-11-…" -> routed ["qa-busy","worker-busy","worker-holder"]
task-1 still assigned to: worker-holder WORKING
#governors-filtered chat_wait woke early: true ["🔌 worker-holder reloading (wrapper_rest"]
Tests 1 failed (1)

FIX DIRECTION
Classify the hold banner as a routine presence line: add its exact daemon-written shape to isRoutinePresenceLine in util/chatPayload.ts. Anchor it the way QUIET_DEREGISTER_BANNER is anchored, so that text appended to a hold banner (and any release or drop banner) keeps routing. Pin the new shape in tools/chatSystemFeed.test.ts next to the task-48edc21b cases. Leave the banner text in workerLifecycle.ts unchanged unless the anchor needs it. Keep the existing error handling: banner posts never block a deregister.
Files: packages/moe-daemon/src/util/chatPayload.ts and packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/chatSystemFeed.test.ts.
definitionOfDone: A wrapper_restart deregister of a task-holding seat (the reload hold) posts banners in #workers and #governors that route to [], add no unread for any seat (the holder included), and do not wake a #governors-filtered chat_wait. A vitest case in tools/chatSystemFeed.test.ts asserts all three.

isRoutinePresenceLine accepts the exact hold-banner shape. It still rejects a banner that released tasks or dropped resource claims, and a hold-banner line with extra text appended. Unit cases in the same test file cover each.
The existing chatSystemFeed, reloadHold and mentionRouter suites pass unchanged, run in a snapshot outside the shared checkout.

implementationPlan.note: RED proof (snapshot /tmp/snap-13ff, vitest on chatSystemFeed.test.ts): 4 failed|26 passed — (h1) and (h2) x3 fail; (h3),(h4) already pass.
GREEN: chatSystemFeed 30/30 pass in snapshot; grep -c u{1F50C} = 2.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: The daemon's reload-hold banner is a routine presence line. state/workerLifecycle.ts beginReloadHold posts it to #workers and #governors in this shape: `🔌 <id> reloading (wrapper_restart); holding N task(s) for its relaunch until <iso>: <taskId>(<STATUS>), …`. It is routed to nobody: no seat gets an unread count, the reloading seat included, and no chat_wait wakes, channel-filtered or not. Agents' chat_read, chat_resync and the chat_wait drain hide it unless includeSystem: true, and the IDE still shows it. Release banners, dropped-claim banners, and a hold banner with anything appended or another reason keep routing as today.
invariants: isRoutinePresenceLine stays total: non-strings return false, no input throws, and matching stays linear on 50000-char input.
A system line with any at-mention is never feed (isSystemFeedMessage is unchanged).
A deregistration banner that released a task or dropped a resource claim still routes to busy seats; that includes the reload_hold_expired one.
compatibility: No ChatMessage schema, wire shape or MCP tool contract changes. Only the set of daemon lines that count as feed changes. Stored legacy hold banners become hidden from agent reads too, as task-48edc21b did for the other presence lines.
util/ keeps no import from state/.
reuse: Extends util/chatPayload.ts isRoutinePresenceLine (task-48edc21b) with one more anchored regex, with no per-caller filter.
sourceAssumptions: state/workerLifecycle.ts:202 beginReloadHold builds the banner from: worker.id; reason, always RELOAD_HOLD_REASON = 'wrapper_restart' (:19, :188); held.length; holdUntil = new Date(...).toISOString(); and tasks.map(task => `${task.id}(${task.status})`).join(', ').

state/chatStore.ts:231 sendMessage sets routingTargets = [] when isSystemFeedMessage is true. tools/chatWait.ts:172 isRelevant and getMessages hideSystemFeed (chatStore.ts:340) use the same predicate.
state/reloadHold.test.ts:77 mocks postToRoleChannel and asserts only the banner text, so a routing change cannot affect it.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) A persisted feed flag on ChatMessage. Rejected: it needs a schema change, and legacy stored lines would stay visible (mem:decision-chat-system-feed-presence-lines). (2) Excluding only the reloading seat from routing. Rejected: the DoD needs [] for every seat. (3) A loose 'reloading (' prefix match. Rejected: appended text and any other reason must keep routing. (4) Importing RELOAD_HOLD_REASON into util. Rejected: util must not depend on state; (h1) drives the real producer instead.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: isSystemFeedMessage in util/chatPayload.ts is the single predicate behind three behaviours: sendMessage's empty routingTargets (no unread, no wake), chat_wait's isRelevant, and every agent read's hideSystemFeed. MentionRouter sends a mention-less system line to every non-IDLE, non-DEAD seat, so before this fix the hold banner reached worker-busy and the reloading worker-holder itself (repro output /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-8f18d6fa/repro-output-util-99cae90a.txt:127-133). The hold path posts no 'left' lines. A hold that runs out is a full reload_hold_expired deregister, and its release banner keeps routing, so the actionable event still pages. The architect dry-ran the regex on 13 accept/reject cases plus long adversarial inputs (1 ms total), and dry-ran the step-3 command at 40c82161: 236 files, 7014 passed, 24 skipped.
planningNotes.risks: The Edit tool may turn \u{1F50C} into a raw plug character. That is harmless under the u flag, but check it with the grep in step 2. The regex is coupled to the producer's wording, and (h1) is the guard: never weaken it to a hand-written string that skips deregisterWorkerTool. Do not edit util/chatPayload.test.ts or any existing chatSystemFeed case (DoD 3). In test strings, build at-signs at runtime.
